additional_info.subject: 0405211 - ID0405211-DC/Si-D/FR-[C0xmCs]- Delivering less power CRM:00472000268
additional_info.body:
Hello Theo,
I have looked at the logs and could identify the root-cause. There is behavior from some truck brands (I know at least from Volvo), that during the charging session they drop the power request and raise the request again during a short period of time. The problem is that after a drop request we never raise back the available power again. This is something that we start to observed now, so the logic in our charger was to react immediately to power drop request. We have report this already to our R&D team and in a future release we will delay the power allocation to avoid cutting power to the EVs in those cases.
If you agree we will proceed to close this case since the problem was identified and there is already a plan for a fix.
With best regards,
Joao Francisco Louro Cardoso

additional_info.subject: RE: 0405211 - ID0405211-DC/Si-D/FR-[C0xmCs]- Delivering less power CRM:00472000268
additional_info.body:
Hello Theo,
Sorry for my delay here. I was waiting for feedback from my colleagues because we have a customer with some Volvo Trucks and we tried to run the tests with them. In fact we did the tests but the trucks were updated with the latest FW from Volvo and the new FW doesn't do this power reduce request as 80%. So there was possibility to test this plug out and plug in at 80%. The good side of this is that at least from Volvo trucks this issue is solved for now.
Are you having issues with other brands as well? I'm available in case you want to do or discuss some tests. Let me know how do you want to proceed or if we close this topic?
